skill_draft.name: differentiate_eosinophilic_lung_patterns
skill_draft.description: When interpreting chest imaging with peripheral opacities in a patient with asthma or eosinophilia, distinguish between Chronic Eosinophilic Pneumonia (CEP) and EGPA based on specific radiographic features and systemic involvement.
skill_draft.applicable_conditions: Chest imaging interpretation tasks involving pulmonary infiltrates, specifically when differential diagnosis includes eosinophilic lung diseases or vasculitis.
skill_draft.core_action: If the imaging shows peripheral, patchy lower-zone or upper-zone opacities (often described as 'photographic negative of pulmonary edema') in the context of asthma/eosinophilia: (1) Prioritize Chronic Eosinophilic Pneumonia (CEP) as the primary differential; (2) Do NOT default to EGPA unless there is explicit evidence of systemic vasculitis (e.g., neuropathy, sinusitis, renal involvement) or specific vascular signs (nodules, cavities); (3) Explicitly state that EGPA is a systemic vasculitis with non-specific pulmonary findings compared to the classic radiographic pattern of CEP.
